overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: emailing a draft decision to a quorum before the meeting was distribution of a document, not deliberation. Claims about evidence accuracy were declined as outside OML.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting when the chair's draft decision was emailed to all members about eight hours before the January 24 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Here, Ms. Hoffman’s e-mail did no more than distribute a document to be discussed at the Board’s meeting that night.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the draft decision misrepresented evidence from the public hearings; the AG was asked to consider that point.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government is charged specifically with reviewing complaints to determine compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, thus we decline to review, and offer no opinion on, whether any actions taken by the Board could be a violation of any other law or regulation pertaining to public hearings.
